q: A railway servant who resigns from service is entitled to the cash equivalent of the Leave on Average Pay standing at his credit on the date of resignation to the extent of:

options.A: The full leave at his credit, subject to a maximum of 300 days
options.B: One-fourth of the leave at his credit, subject to a maximum of 75 days
options.C: Half of the leave at his credit, subject to a maximum of 150 days
options.D: No encashment is admissible on resignation

e: On resignation, cash equivalent of LAP is admissible for half of the leave at credit, subject to a maximum of 150 days, under the leave rules.

q: In regard to Children Education Allowance and Hostel Subsidy for one and the same child, the correct position is that a railway servant can claim:

options.A: Both Children Education Allowance and Hostel Subsidy together for the same child
options.B: Only one of the two, that is, either Children Education Allowance or Hostel Subsidy, for the same child
options.C: Hostel Subsidy in addition to Children Education Allowance at double the rate
options.D: Neither of them where the child is residing in a hostel

e: For the same child, only one of Children Education Allowance or Hostel Subsidy can be claimed, not both together.

q: The Payment of Wages Act, 1936 applies to an employed person whose wages do not exceed:

options.A: Rs 10,000 per month
options.B: Rs 18,000 per month
options.C: Rs 21,000 per month
options.D: Rs 24,000 per month

e:
The Payment of Wages Act, 1936 applies to an employed person whose wages do not exceed Rs 24,000 per month.
Update: under the Code on Wages, 2019 - in force w.e.f. 21.11.2025, subsuming the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 - there is no wage ceiling: the code applies to all employees irrespective of wages. (Source: Code on Wages, 2019, Ministry of Labour & Employment; PIB press release dated 21.11.2025.)

q: The amount of insurance cover admissible to the family of a Group 'D' (Level-1) railway servant who dies while in service, under the Central Government Employees Group Insurance Scheme, is:
e: Under CGEGIS, the insurance cover for a Group D (Level-1) servant dying in service is Rs 15,000, matching the Rs 15 monthly subscription slab.

q: The Special Allowance for Child Care admissible to a woman railway servant with disability, in respect of her two eldest surviving children from their birth till they attain the age of two years, is payable at the rate of:

options.A: Rs 1,000 per month
options.B: Rs 1,500 per month
options.C: Rs 3,750 per month
options.D: Rs 2,250 per month

e: Special Allowance for Child Care for a woman servant with disability is Rs 3,000 per month, raised by 25 percent when DA crossed 50 percent, i.e. Rs 3,750 per month, for the two eldest surviving children up to age two.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A gazetted railway servant classified as 'Excluded' under the Hours of Employment Regulations is entitled to Overtime Allowance at twice the ordinary rate of pay.
2. Overtime Allowance is payable to eligible railway servants for duty performed by them beyond their rostered hours of work.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Excluded category staff are not entitled to overtime at double rate, so statement 1 is wrong; overtime allowance is payable to eligible staff for duty beyond rostered hours, so only statement 2 is correct.

q: 'Information', as defined in the Right to Information Act, 2005, includes:

options.A: Only printed records and documents held by the public authority
options.B: Only data material held in electronic form
options.C: Opinions and advices, but not samples and models
options.D: Records, documents, memos, e-mails, opinions, advices, press releases, circulars, orders, logbooks, contracts, reports, papers, samples, models and data material held in any form

e: Section 2(f) of the RTI Act defines information widely to include records, documents, memos, e-mails, opinions, advices, press releases, circulars, orders, logbooks, contracts, reports, papers, samples, models and data in any form.

q: A railway servant who retains a railway quarter allotted to him beyond the permissible period, without the permission of the competent authority, is liable to pay for the period of such unauthorised occupation:

options.A: Damage rent
options.B: Normal licence fee only
options.C: No charges, as the quarter was allotted to him in service
options.D: Only the House Rent Allowance drawn by him for that period

e: Unauthorised retention of a railway quarter beyond the permissible period, without permission, makes the servant liable to pay damage rent for that period.

q: Under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, a deduction made from the wages of an employed person on account of his absence from duty shall not exceed:

options.A: The whole of the wages for the wage period
options.B: An amount bearing the same proportion to the wages payable for the wage period as the period of absence bears to that wage period
options.C: Fifty per cent of the wages for the wage period in all cases
options.D: Three days' wages, irrespective of the period of absence

e: Section 9 of the Payment of Wages Act limits deduction for absence to an amount bearing the same proportion to wages for the wage period as the period of absence bears to that period.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding Transport Allowance:
1. Transport Allowance is admissible at double the normal rate to Divyangjan railway servants.
2. The rates of Transport Allowance are prescribed with reference to the pay level of the railway servant and the classification of the city in which he is posted.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Transport Allowance is payable at double the normal rate to Divyangjan servants, and its rates are prescribed with reference to pay level and the classification of the city of posting, so both statements are correct.

q: A railway servant retires from service on 31st December, 2026 and his annual increment falls due on 1st January, 2027. For the purpose of his pensionary benefits, he is entitled to:

options.A: No increment, as he was not in service on the date on which the increment fell due
options.B: Two notional increments by way of compensation
options.C: A notional increment only if he has completed 33 years of qualifying service
options.D: One notional increment, as if it had been drawn by him before his retirement

e: A servant retiring on 31 December whose increment falls due on 1 January is entitled to one notional increment for pensionary benefits, as if drawn before retirement.

q: A candidate is appointed to a post on the Railways on 20th March, 2026. He will draw his first annual increment on:

options.A: 1st January, 2027
options.B: 1st July, 2026
options.C: 20th March, 2027
options.D: 1st July, 2027

e: An increment is due only after six months of service on 1 January or 1 July; appointed on 20 March 2026, he has under six months by 1 July 2026, so his first increment falls on 1 January 2027.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation with 200 days of Leave on Average Pay at his credit. His basic pay at retirement is Rs 50,000 per month and Dearness Allowance is admissible at 50%. The cash equivalent of leave salary payable to him is:
e: Cash equivalent = (pay plus DA) / 30 x days of LAP: (Rs 50,000 + Rs 25,000) / 30 x 200 = Rs 75,000 / 30 x 200 = Rs 5,00,000.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after rendering 20 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 60,000 per month. The retirement gratuity payable to him will be:
e: Retirement gratuity is one-fourth of emoluments per six-monthly period: 20 years = 40 periods, 40 x 1/4 = 10 months, 10 x Rs 60,000 = Rs 6,00,000, within the 16.5 times ceiling.

q: A railway pensioner's monthly pension is Rs 20,000. He commutes 40 per cent of his pension. Taking the commutation value for his age on the next birthday as 8.194 for each rupee of annual pension commuted, the lump sum commuted value payable to him will be:
e: Commuted portion is 40 percent of Rs 20,000 = Rs 8,000 per month, i.e. Rs 96,000 per year; lump sum = Rs 96,000 x 8.194 = Rs 7,86,624.

q: A railway servant covered under the National Pension System draws basic pay of Rs 40,000 per month and Dearness Allowance at 50 per cent. The monthly contribution payable by the Government to his Tier-I account will be:
e: Government NPS contribution is 14 percent of Basic Pay plus DA: (Rs 40,000 + Rs 20,000) x 14/100 = Rs 60,000 x 14/100 = Rs 8,400 per month.

q: 'Time scale pay', as defined in the Fundamental Rules applicable to railway servants, means:

options.A: The pay to which a railway servant is entitled on account of a post to which he has been appointed substantively
options.B: Pay which, subject to any condition prescribed in the rules, rises by periodical increments from a minimum to a maximum
options.C: Additional pay granted to a railway servant to save him from a loss of substantive pay
options.D: An addition to the emoluments of a post granted in consideration of the specially arduous nature of the duties

e: Under the Fundamental Rules, time scale pay is pay which, subject to prescribed conditions, rises by periodical increments from a minimum to a maximum.

q: Under the pension rules applicable to railway servants, the term 'pension' is understood to:

options.A: Mean only the monthly pension and never to include gratuity
options.B: Include family pension but not gratuity in any case
options.C: Include gratuity also, except where the term is used in contradistinction to gratuity
options.D: Include the balance at the credit of the railway servant in the Provident Fund

e: Under the RS (Pension) Rules, the term pension includes gratuity also, except where it is used in contradistinction to gratuity.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Casual leave is debited to the leave account of a railway servant.
2. Sundays and holidays falling during a spell of casual leave are counted as casual leave.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Casual leave is not debited to the leave account, and Sundays and holidays falling during casual leave are not counted as casual leave, so neither statement is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Retirement gratuity is admissible to a railway servant only if he has completed a minimum qualifying service of five years.
2. Death gratuity is not admissible to the family of a railway servant who dies in service before completing five years of qualifying service.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Retirement gratuity requires a minimum qualifying service of five years, so statement 1 is correct; death gratuity is admissible even before five years (2x, 6x slabs etc.), so statement 2 is wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding joining time:
1. The joining time admissible to a railway servant on transfer in public interest includes six days for preparation, in addition to the time required for the journey.
2. Joining time is not admissible to a railway servant where the transfer is made at his own request.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Joining time includes six days for preparation plus journey time, and it is not admissible where the transfer is at the servant's own request, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. House Rent Allowance is admissible to a railway servant who has been allotted, and is in occupation of, a railway quarter.
2. For the purpose of House Rent Allowance, cities are classified as 'X', 'Y' and 'Z' on the basis of their population.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: HRA is not admissible to a servant allotted and occupying a railway quarter, so statement 1 is wrong; cities are classified X, Y and Z by population for HRA, so only statement 2 is correct.

q: Withholding of increments of pay with cumulative effect, as a penalty, differs from withholding of increments without cumulative effect in that, in the former case:

options.A: The penalty can be imposed only by the Railway Board
options.B: No departmental inquiry is required before imposing the penalty
options.C: The railway servant is also debarred from promotion permanently
options.D: The increments withheld are not restored on the expiry of the penalty period, so that the penalty has a permanent effect on the pay, and consequently on the pension, of the railway servant

e: Withholding of increments with cumulative effect permanently postpones future increments, so the withheld increments are not restored on expiry of the penalty and pay and pension remain affected.

q: The provision of the Right to Information Act, 2005 which gives the Act an overriding effect over the Official Secrets Act, 1923 and any other law for the time being in force is:

options.A: Section 22
options.B: Section 24
options.C: Section 31
options.D: Section 8

e: Section 22 of the RTI Act, 2005 gives the Act overriding effect over the Official Secrets Act, 1923 and any other law in force.

q: Where a request for information under the Right to Information Act, 2005 relates to information supplied by a third party and treated as confidential by that third party, the Central Public Information Officer shall give a written notice to the third party within:

options.A: 10 days of the receipt of the request
options.B: 5 days of the receipt of the request
options.C: 15 days of the receipt of the request
options.D: 30 days of the receipt of the request

e: Under Section 11 of the RTI Act, where third party confidential information is involved, the CPIO must give written notice to the third party within 5 days of receipt of the request.

q: Appointments on compassionate grounds on the Railways are normally made only in:

options.A: Group 'A' and Group 'B' gazetted posts
options.B: Any post, including gazetted posts, according to the qualification of the candidate
options.C: Group 'C' posts and erstwhile Group 'D' (Level-1) posts
options.D: Work-charged posts only

e: Appointments on compassionate grounds are normally made only in Group C posts and erstwhile Group D (Level-1) posts.

q: Under the 7th CPC dispensation, City Compensatory Allowance admissible earlier to railway servants has been:

options.A: Doubled for servants posted in 'X' class cities
options.B: Retained at the pre-revised rates
options.C: Merged with Transport Allowance
options.D: Abolished, its purpose having been subsumed in the House Rent Allowance

e: City Compensatory Allowance stands abolished under the 7th CPC, its purpose being subsumed in House Rent Allowance.

q: The prescribed benchmark of grading in the Annual Performance Appraisal Report for regular promotion of a railway servant, other than a financial upgradation under the MACP scheme, is:

options.A: 'Good'
options.B: 'Very Good'
options.C: 'Outstanding'
options.D: 'Average'

e: The APAR benchmark for regular promotion is Good; Very Good is the benchmark prescribed for MACP financial upgradation.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Dress Allowance is paid to eligible railway servants once in a year, in the month of July.
2. The erstwhile Washing Allowance stands subsumed in the Dress Allowance under the 7th CPC dispensation.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Dress Allowance is paid once a year in July to eligible servants, and the erstwhile Washing Allowance stands subsumed in it under the 7th CPC, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Reservation for persons with benchmark disabilities in direct recruitment on the Railways is 3 per cent of the vacancies.
2. Reservation for persons with benchmark disabilities is a horizontal reservation, which cuts across the vertical categories of reservation.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Reservation for persons with benchmark disabilities is 4 percent, not 3 percent, so statement 1 is wrong; it is a horizontal reservation cutting across vertical categories, so only statement 2 is correct.

q: Under the Right to Information (Fee and Cost) Rules, the fee chargeable for providing information on a compact disc is:

options.A: Rs 10 per disc
options.B: Rs 100 per disc
options.C: Rs 2 per disc
options.D: Rs 50 per disc

e: Under the RTI (Fee and Cost) Rules, the fee for providing information on a compact disc is Rs 50 per disc.

q: Extra Ordinary Leave may be granted to a railway servant even in a case where other leave is admissible to him, provided that:

options.A: He applies for the grant of such leave in writing
options.B: He has completed not less than 20 years of service
options.C: He surrenders the Leave on Average Pay at his credit
options.D: The Railway Board sanctions the leave in each such case

e: EOL may be granted even when other leave is admissible, provided the railway servant applies for it in writing.

q: The restricted holidays admissible to a railway servant in a calendar year are availed of by him:

options.A: On any two days of his own choice, whether or not they are holidays
options.B: From the list of restricted holidays notified by the office for that year
options.C: Only by converting two days of his casual leave
options.D: Only on the festivals of the religion professed by him, with the sanction of the Railway Board

e: Restricted holidays, two in a calendar year, can be availed only from the list of restricted holidays notified by the office for that year.

q: The employees working in a statutory canteen provided in a railway workshop under the Factories Act, 1948 are treated as:

options.A: Employees of the contractor running the canteen
options.B: Casual labour engaged by the workshop
options.C: Railway servants
options.D: Act Apprentices of the workshop

e: Employees of a statutory canteen provided under the Factories Act, 1948 in a railway workshop are treated as railway servants.

q: 'Public authority', as defined in the Right to Information Act, 2005, includes a body or institution which is:

options.A: A Government department only
options.B: Created by or under the Constitution only
options.C: Employing more than one hundred persons only
options.D: Owned, controlled or substantially financed, directly or indirectly, by funds provided by the appropriate Government

e: Section 2(h) of the RTI Act includes in public authority any body or institution owned, controlled or substantially financed, directly or indirectly, by funds provided by the appropriate Government.

q: Recognition of trade unions at the zonal railway level on the Railways is decided through:

options.A: Elections held by secret ballot among the employees
options.B: Nomination by the General Manager of the Railway
options.C: Verification of membership from subscription records alone
options.D: Selection by the Railway Board from among the applicant unions

e: Recognition of trade unions at the zonal railway level is decided through elections held by secret ballot among the employees.

q: Which of the following matters is NOT ordinarily taken up in the Permanent Negotiating Machinery on the Railways?

options.A: Matters relating to the conditions of service of staff generally
options.B: An individual grievance of a particular railway servant
options.C: Welfare measures affecting railway employees as a class
options.D: Matters of general importance arising between the Administration and the recognised federations

e: The PNM deals with matters of general importance, conditions of service and welfare of staff as a class; an individual grievance of a particular servant is not ordinarily taken up in it.

q:
Consider the following statements under the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops:
1. No adult worker shall be required or allowed to work in a factory for more than nine hours in any day.
2. Where a worker works for more than nine hours in a day or for more than forty-eight hours in a week, he is entitled to wages at twice his ordinary rate of wages in respect of the overtime work.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Section 51 and 54 of the Factories Act bar work beyond 48 hours a week and 9 hours a day, and Section 59 gives wages at twice the ordinary rate for overtime, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Leave Not Due can be granted to a railway servant without the production of a medical certificate.
2. Leave Not Due granted to a railway servant is debited against the Leave on Average Pay which he will earn in future.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Leave Not Due is granted only on medical certificate (or in specified continuation cases), so statement 1 is wrong; it is debited against future Leave on Half Average Pay, not Leave on Average Pay, so statement 2 is also wrong.

q: Family pension admissible to the family of a deceased railway servant is payable in the first instance to:

options.A: The dependent parents of the deceased railway servant
options.B: The widow or widower of the deceased railway servant
options.C: The eldest son of the deceased railway servant
options.D: The eldest daughter of the deceased railway servant

e: Under the RS (Pension) Rules, family pension is payable in the first instance to the widow or widower of the deceased railway servant.

q: Apart from the annual verification and attestation of entries by the Head of Office, the Service Book of a railway servant is also required to be:

options.A: Sent to the Accounts Office every year for safe custody
options.B: Shown to the railway servant concerned every year, and his signature obtained in it in token of his having seen it
options.C: Shown to the railway servant only at the time of his retirement
options.D: Rewritten afresh every five years by the office

e: The Service Book must be shown to the railway servant every year and his signature obtained in token of having seen it, besides annual verification and attestation by the Head of Office.

q: Where the original Service Book of a railway servant is lost, the correct position is that:

options.A: A fresh service record is started from the date of loss, ignoring the earlier service
options.B: The railway servant is treated as a fresh entrant for all purposes
options.C: A duplicate Service Book may be prepared by the Head of Office on the basis of the available records, the past entries being verified and reconstructed as far as possible
options.D: No duplicate Service Book can be prepared under any circumstances

e: If the original Service Book is lost, a duplicate may be prepared by the Head of Office from available records, with past entries verified and reconstructed as far as possible.

q: A railway servant cannot be transferred to foreign service:

options.A: Against his will
options.B: For a period exceeding one year in any case
options.C: Unless he has completed twenty years of service
options.D: Unless he holds a gazetted post

e: A railway servant cannot be transferred to foreign service against his will, as foreign service requires his consent under the Fundamental Rules.

q: Training Allowance, admissible under the 7th CPC dispensation, is payable to:

options.A: Every railway servant who undergoes a departmental training course
options.B: Railway servants who are paid a stipend during their initial training
options.C: Only the trainees residing in the hostels of training institutes
options.D: The faculty members, that is, the instructors posted in the training institutions of the Railways, in consideration of their instructional duties

e: Training Allowance under the 7th CPC is payable to faculty members, i.e. instructors posted in railway training institutions, for their instructional duties.

q: The contributions towards pension and leave salary in respect of a railway servant are required to be recovered from the borrowing authority only where the railway servant is:

options.A: On deputation to another department of the Government, his service counting for pension in his parent cadre without any such contribution
options.B: On foreign service, that is, service in which he receives his pay from a source other than the revenues of the Government or of the Railways
options.C: Transferred from one zonal Railway to another in public interest
options.D: Appointed to an ex-cadre post within his own Railway

e: Pension and leave salary contributions are recovered from the borrowing authority only for foreign service, where pay comes from a source other than Government or Railway revenues.

q: 'Current charge' of a higher post held by a railway servant, in addition to his own duties, differs from 'full additional charge' of that post in that, in the former case, the railway servant:

options.A: Draws the full pay of the higher post for the period of the arrangement
options.B: Discharges all the duties of the higher post, including its statutory functions
options.C: Looks after only the day-to-day routine work of the higher post and does not discharge its statutory functions
options.D: Is deemed to have been promoted to the higher post for all purposes

e: In current charge, the servant looks after only day-to-day routine work of the higher post and does not discharge its statutory functions, unlike full additional charge.

q: In the Annual Performance Appraisal Report of a railway servant, the assessment recorded by the Reporting Officer is thereafter:

options.A: Reviewed by the Reviewing Officer and accepted by the Accepting Authority
options.B: Sent directly to the Railway Board for final grading
options.C: Recorded afresh by the Accounts Office
options.D: Communicated to the recognised trade union of the cadre

e: In APAR, the Reporting Officer's assessment is reviewed by the Reviewing Officer and then accepted by the Accepting Authority.

q: Under the Indian Railway Establishment Manual, a railway servant may represent against his position as shown in the published seniority list of his category within:

options.A: One month
options.B: Three months
options.C: One year
options.D: Five years

e: Under IREM, a representation against the position in a published seniority list must be made within one year of its publication.

q: In regard to the investment of the accumulations in his Tier-I account, a Government subscriber under the National Pension System:

options.A: Has no say of any kind in the matter at any stage
options.B: Is permitted to choose the Pension Fund and the investment pattern for his contributions, from among the options prescribed in this behalf
options.C: May invest the entire amount directly in the share market through a broker of his choice
options.D: May withdraw the accumulations and invest them in a deposit of his choice

e: A Government NPS subscriber may choose the Pension Fund and the investment pattern for his contributions from among the options prescribed for Government subscribers.

q: In regard to the balance at the credit of a subscriber in the General Provident Fund, the correct position is that the subscriber:

options.A: Is furnished with a statement of his Provident Fund account once a year, after the accounts for the year are closed, showing the opening balance, the amounts credited and debited, the interest credited and the closing balance
options.B: Is never informed of the balance at his credit during his service
options.C: Can ascertain his balance only at the time of his retirement
options.D: Is furnished with a statement of his account only on his transfer to another Railway

e: The GPF subscriber is furnished a statement of account once a year after the year's accounts are closed, showing opening balance, credits, debits, interest and closing balance.

q: A subscriber to the General Provident Fund who wishes to reduce the amount of his monthly subscription during the course of a financial year may do so:

options.A: At any time and as often as he likes
options.B: Not at all, as the subscription once fixed can only be enhanced
options.C: Only once during the course of the financial year
options.D: Only with the prior approval of the Railway Board

e: A GPF subscriber may reduce the amount of his monthly subscription only once during the course of a financial year.

q: The service record of a railway servant, corresponding to the Service Book, is now maintained on the Railways in electronic form as:

options.A: The e-PPO in the ARPAN portal
options.B: A scanned file kept in the divisional office
options.C: A register maintained by the Accounts Office
options.D: The e-Service Book in the Human Resource Management System (HRMS)

e: The service record corresponding to the Service Book is now maintained electronically as the e-Service Book in HRMS.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding a period of unauthorised absence of a railway servant:
1. No pay is admissible to him for the period, the period being treated as 'dies non', not counting for increment or pension.
2. Unauthorised absence also renders the railway servant liable to disciplinary action for misconduct.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Unauthorised absence is treated as dies non with no pay, not counting for increment or pension, and also renders the servant liable to disciplinary action, so both statements are correct.

q: The Internal Complaints Committee constituted in a railway office to enquire into complaints of sexual harassment of women employees at the workplace is required to have:

options.A: The head of the office as its Presiding Officer in every case
options.B: A woman employee at a senior level as its Presiding Officer, and at least one member from outside the office, drawn from a non-governmental organisation or association committed to the cause of women or familiar with the issues of sexual harassment
options.C: Only officers of the Personnel Branch as its members
options.D: A representative of the Railway Board as its Presiding Officer

e: Under the POSH Act, the Internal Complaints Committee must have a woman employee at senior level as Presiding Officer and at least one external member from an NGO or association committed to the cause of women or familiar with sexual harassment issues.

q: The maximum amount of monthly pension admissible to a railway pensioner under the 7th CPC dispensation is:

options.A: Rs 1,12,500 per month
options.B: Rs 90,000 per month
options.C: Rs 1,25,000 per month in all cases, including the Railways
options.D: There is no ceiling on the amount of pension

e: Maximum pension is 50 percent of the highest pay of Rs 2,50,000 under the 7th CPC, i.e. Rs 1,25,000 per month, applicable including on the Railways.

q: The minimum amount of family pension admissible to the family of a deceased railway servant under the 7th CPC dispensation is:

options.A: Rs 3,500 per month
options.B: Rs 7,000 per month
options.C: Rs 12,500 per month
options.D: Rs 9,000 per month

e: The minimum family pension under the 7th CPC dispensation is fixed at Rs 9,000 per month, plus dearness relief thereon.

q: For the timely preparation of pension papers, every Head of Office on the Railways is required to have a list prepared, of all railway servants who are due to retire within the next twelve to fifteen months:

options.A: Once in five years
options.B: Every three months, on the 1st January, 1st April, 1st July and 1st October, and to forward a copy of the list to the Accounts Officer
options.C: Only in the month of January every year
options.D: Only when the Railway Board calls for such a list

e: For timely pension papers, the Head of Office must prepare the list of servants due to retire in the next 12 to 15 months every three months, on 1 January, 1 April, 1 July and 1 October, and forward a copy to the Accounts Officer.

q: On the retirement of a railway servant, the pension, gratuity and commutation admissible to him are authorised for payment by:

options.A: The pension disbursing bank, on its own verification of the service records
options.B: The Head of Office himself, without any check by the Accounts Office
options.C: The Accounts Officer, who, after verification of the qualifying service and the emoluments of the railway servant, issues the Pension Payment Order
options.D: The Railway Board in every case

e: On retirement, pension, gratuity and commutation are authorised by the Accounts Officer, who verifies qualifying service and emoluments and issues the Pension Payment Order.

q: A railway pensioner commuted a portion of his pension at the time of his retirement, and the commuted portion has since been restored to him on the expiry of fifteen years. He now applies for commutation of a portion of his pension afresh. The correct position is that:

options.A: Fresh commutation of the restored portion of pension is not permissible
options.B: He may commute up to 40 per cent of his pension afresh, as a matter of right
options.C: He may commute the restored portion after undergoing a medical examination
options.D: He may commute the restored portion with the sanction of the Railway Board

e: Fresh commutation of pension is not permissible after the commuted portion has been restored on expiry of fifteen years.

q: A railway pensioner applied for commutation of a portion of his pension in time, and the commutation became absolute, but he died before the lump sum commuted value could actually be paid to him. In regard to the commuted value, the correct position is that:

options.A: The amount lapses to the Railways
options.B: Only one-half of the amount is payable to his family
options.C: The amount is adjusted against the family pension payable to his family
options.D: The commuted value is payable to his family or nominee, as the commutation had already become absolute

e: Where commutation had become absolute before death, the lump sum commuted value is payable to the family or nominee and does not lapse.

q: An ex-serviceman re-employed on the Railways, who is in receipt of a military pension for his earlier military service, wishes that service to be counted as qualifying service for pension in civil service. He may be permitted to do so if he:

options.A: Continues to draw the military pension in full and also counts the same service again
options.B: Ceases to draw the military pension and refunds the pension and gratuity drawn by him in respect of that military service, in accordance with the prescribed conditions
options.C: Merely intimates his option to his office, without any refund
options.D: Has completed not less than twenty years of military service

e: An ex-serviceman may count military service for civil pension only if he ceases to draw military pension and refunds the pension and gratuity drawn for that service, as per prescribed conditions.

q: Under the Unified Pension Scheme, the assured payout is NOT admissible to a subscriber who:

options.A: Retires on superannuation after completing the prescribed qualifying service
options.B: Retires voluntarily in accordance with the provisions of the scheme
options.C: Is dismissed or removed from service, or resigns from service, except in the circumstances specially prescribed
options.D: Dies while in service, his family being denied any benefit in every such case

e: Under UPS, assured payout is not admissible to a subscriber who is dismissed or removed from service, or who resigns, except in specially prescribed circumstances.

q: Where family pension becomes payable to twin children of a deceased railway servant, it is paid to them:

options.A: In equal shares
options.B: Wholly to the elder of the twins
options.C: Wholly to the younger of the twins
options.D: In shares proportionate to their ages

e: Where family pension is payable to twin children, it is paid to them in equal shares.

q: The additional quantum of pension admissible to a railway pensioner on his attaining the age of 80 years and above is payable to him:

options.A: From the first day of the year following the year in which he attains that age
options.B: From the first day of the month in which he attains that age
options.C: Only from the date on which he submits an application for it
options.D: Only after a fresh Pension Payment Order is issued on his next birthday

e: Additional quantum of pension on attaining 80 years is payable from the first day of the month in which the pensioner attains that age.

q: Where only the year of birth of a person entering railway service is known, and neither the month nor the date of birth is known, the date of birth to be recorded in his service records is taken as:

options.A: The 1st January of that year
options.B: The 31st December of that year
options.C: The 15th August of that year
options.D: The 1st July of that year

e: Where only the year of birth is known, the date of birth is recorded as 1 July of that year for service records.

q: A railway servant retires from service after rendering 6 years of qualifying service and is accordingly not entitled to pension. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 30,000 per month. The service gratuity payable to him, at half a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: Service gratuity for service under 10 years is half a month's emoluments per six-monthly period: 6 years = 12 periods, 12 x 1/2 = 6 months, 6 x Rs 30,000 = Rs 1,80,000.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 10 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of his death are Rs 50,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family, at twelve times the emoluments, as admissible for this length of service, will be:
e: Death gratuity for 10 years qualifying service falls in the 5 to 11 years slab at 12 times emoluments: 12 x Rs 50,000 = Rs 6,00,000.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after rendering 25 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 72,000 per month. The retirement gratuity payable to him, at one-fourth of a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: Retirement gratuity is one-fourth of emoluments per six-monthly period: 25 years = 50 periods, 50 x 1/4 = 12.5 months, 12.5 x Rs 72,000 = Rs 9,00,000, within the 16.5 times ceiling.

q: In accordance with the policy of the Government regarding the posting of spouses, where both the husband and the wife are in Government service, they should, as far as administratively possible, be:

options.A: Posted at different stations, to avoid any conflict of interest
options.B: Posted in different Railways in every case
options.C: Allowed to serve together only after completing ten years of service
options.D: Posted at the same station, so that they can lead a normal family life

e: As per Government spouse-posting policy, husband and wife in Government service should, as far as administratively possible, be posted at the same station to lead a normal family life.

q: The General Departmental Competitive Examination (GDCE) held on the Railways is a scheme under which:

options.A: Serving railway employees who fulfil the prescribed qualifications and age conditions are permitted to compete for a specified proportion of the vacancies in the direct recruitment quota of certain posts
options.B: Only candidates from the open market can appear
options.C: Railway employees are promoted to higher posts without any examination
options.D: Serving railway employees can compete for gazetted posts of all departments without any condition

e: GDCE is a scheme under which serving railway employees fulfilling prescribed qualifications and age conditions may compete for a specified proportion of direct recruitment quota vacancies in certain posts.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding trade unions of railway servants:
1. A trade union of railway servants is registered under the Trade Unions Act, 1926.
2. Registration of a union under that Act does not by itself entitle the union to recognition by the Railway Administration, recognition being governed separately by the instructions of the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: A railway trade union is registered under the Trade Unions Act, 1926, but registration alone does not give recognition, which is governed separately by Railway instructions, so both statements are correct.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to railway workshops, a Safety Officer is required to be appointed in a factory in which the number of workers ordinarily employed is:

options.A: Two hundred and fifty or more
options.B: One thousand or more
options.C: One hundred or more
options.D: Five hundred or more

e: Section 40B of the Factories Act requires appointment of a Safety Officer in a factory where 1,000 or more workers are ordinarily employed.

q: Under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, where none of the deductions made from the wages of an employed person is a payment to a co-operative society, the total amount of deductions that can be made from his wages in any wage period shall not exceed:

options.A: Twenty-five per cent of his wages for that period
options.B: Seventy-five per cent of his wages for that period
options.C: The whole of his wages for that period
options.D: Fifty per cent of his wages for that period

e: Section 7 of the Payment of Wages Act caps total deductions at 50 percent of wages in a wage period, the 75 percent limit applying only where deductions include payments to co-operative societies.

q: A railway servant to whom a railway quarter is allotted occupies it in the capacity of:

options.A: A licensee of the Railways, the allotment being liable to be cancelled in accordance with the rules and creating no right of tenancy in his favour
options.B: A tenant of the Railways, with all the rights of a tenant under the rent control laws
options.C: The owner of the quarter till his retirement
options.D: A lessee under a registered lease deed executed with the Railways

e: A railway servant occupies an allotted quarter only as a licensee; allotment creates no tenancy right and is liable to cancellation under the rules.

q: The type of railway residential accommodation to which a railway servant is entitled is determined primarily with reference to:

options.A: The length of his service
options.B: The size of his family alone
options.C: His pay, that is, the pay level or emoluments drawn by him
options.D: The availability of quarters of any type at the station

e: Entitlement to a type of railway residential accommodation is determined primarily with reference to the pay, i.e. pay level or emoluments, drawn by the servant.

q: A person who continues to occupy a railway quarter after the allotment in his favour has been cancelled, and is thus in unauthorised occupation of it, can be evicted from the quarter in accordance with the provisions of:

options.A: The Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules alone, and no other law
options.B: The Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1971, railway quarters being public premises
options.C: The Transfer of Property Act, after obtaining a decree from a civil court in every case
options.D: No law, as a railway quarter once allotted can never be got vacated

e: Unauthorised occupation of a railway quarter, being public premises, is dealt with by eviction under the Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1971.

q: A railway servant who joins a new post under the Government after tendering a technical resignation from his railway post, with proper permission, is entitled, in the matter of fixation of his pay in the new post, to:

options.A: Fixation at the minimum of the pay level of the new post in every case
options.B: A fresh start, his past pay being wholly ignored
options.C: Protection only if the new post is in a lower pay level
options.D: Protection of the pay last drawn by him in the old post, subject to the maximum of the pay level of the new post

e: On technical resignation and joining a new Government post with proper permission, pay is fixed with protection of the pay last drawn in the old post, subject to the maximum of the pay level of the new post.

q: A railway servant who is ordered to proceed on tour in connection with his official duties may, before proceeding on the tour, draw:

options.A: An advance of travelling allowance, to meet the expenses of the journey, which is adjusted against the travelling allowance claim submitted by him on completion of the tour
options.B: The full travelling allowance for the tour, which is not required to be adjusted in any case
options.C: An advance equal to three months' pay in every case
options.D: No amount of any kind in advance

e: A servant proceeding on tour may draw an advance of travelling allowance to meet journey expenses, adjusted against the TA claim submitted on completion of the tour.

q: The appointment of a person to a post in railway service is made subject to the verification of his character and antecedents. The correct position in this regard is that:

options.A: The verification is carried out only after the person completes his probation
options.B: The verification is never carried out for non-gazetted posts
options.C: The appointment remains provisional until the verification of character and antecedents is completed satisfactorily
options.D: An unsatisfactory report on verification has no effect on the appointment

e: Appointment is provisional until verification of character and antecedents is completed satisfactorily; an unsatisfactory report affects the appointment.

q: The minimum educational qualification ordinarily prescribed for direct recruitment to Level-1 (erstwhile Group 'D') posts on the Railways is:

options.A: A graduate degree from a recognised university
options.B: 10th pass, or ITI, or an equivalent qualification, or the National Apprenticeship Certificate granted by the National Council for Vocational Training
options.C: 12th pass from a recognised board in every case
options.D: No educational qualification at all

e: The minimum qualification ordinarily prescribed for Level-1 posts is 10th pass, or ITI, or equivalent, or National Apprenticeship Certificate granted by NCVT.

q: A person engaged as an Act Apprentice on the Railways for undergoing apprenticeship training is paid, during the period of his training:

options.A: The full pay of the post against which he is engaged
options.B: No amount of any kind
options.C: Only the travelling allowance admissible on tour
options.D: A stipend at the rate prescribed under the Apprentices Act, 1961 and the rules made thereunder

e: An Act Apprentice is paid only a stipend at the rate prescribed under the Apprentices Act, 1961 and rules thereunder during training, not the pay of a post.

q: A railway servant who is re-employed in a Government office after his retirement:

options.A: Continues to draw his pension during the period of his re-employment, the re-employment not by itself suspending or stopping the pension
options.B: Is required to surrender his pension for the whole period of re-employment
options.C: Can draw either his pension or the pay of the re-employed post, but not both in any case
options.D: Forfeits his pension permanently on accepting re-employment

e: A re-employed pensioner continues to draw his pension during re-employment; re-employment by itself does not suspend or stop the pension.

q: Cash equivalent of the Leave on Average Pay standing at the credit of a railway servant is NOT admissible where the railway servant:

options.A: Retires on attaining the age of superannuation
options.B: Takes voluntary retirement in accordance with the rules
options.C: Is dismissed from service as a result of disciplinary proceedings
options.D: Dies while in service, the amount being payable to his family

e: Cash equivalent of LAP is not admissible on dismissal from service; it is admissible on superannuation, voluntary retirement and, to the family, on death in service.

q: In regard to Dearness Relief on family pension, the correct position is that a family pensioner who has taken up employment:

options.A: Is not entitled to Dearness Relief for so long as he or she remains in employment
options.B: Remains entitled to Dearness Relief on the family pension, Dearness Relief being admissible to an employed family pensioner
options.C: Is entitled to Dearness Relief at only one-half of the normal rate
options.D: Must surrender the family pension on taking up employment

e: Dearness Relief on family pension remains admissible even if the family pensioner takes up employment; employment does not bar DR on family pension.

q: Where a worker in a factory governed by the Factories Act, 1948, is required to work on his weekly holiday, he becomes entitled to:

options.A: Double wages for the day, in lieu of the holiday, in every case
options.B: No compensatory benefit of any kind
options.C: Only a cash allowance in lieu of the holiday
options.D: Compensatory holidays, equal in number to the weekly holidays so lost, in accordance with the provisions of the Act

e: Under Section 53 of the Factories Act, a worker deprived of a weekly holiday is entitled to compensatory holidays equal in number to the holidays lost.

q: Leave of a railway servant ordinarily begins and ends as under:

options.A: It begins on the day on which charge is relinquished and ends on the day on which charge is resumed
options.B: It begins on the first day of the month in which it is sanctioned and ends on the last day of that month
options.C: It begins on the day following the day on which charge of the post is relinquished and ends on the day preceding the day on which charge is resumed
options.D: It begins and ends on the dates entered in the leave application, irrespective of the relinquishing or resumption of charge

e: Leave ordinarily begins on the day following the day charge is relinquished and ends on the day preceding the day charge is resumed.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding fixation of pay under Fundamental Rule 22(1)(a):
1. Where the appointment to the new post involves the assumption of duties and responsibilities of greater importance, the pay is fixed at the stage next above the pay drawn by the railway servant in the old post.
2. Where the appointment to the new post does not involve the assumption of duties and responsibilities of greater importance, the pay is fixed at the minimum of the pay level of the new post in all cases.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Under FR 22(1)(a)(1), on appointment involving greater duties and responsibilities, pay is fixed at the stage next above the old pay, so statement 1 is correct; statement 2 is wrong as pay is not fixed at the minimum in all such other cases.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding Travelling Allowance:
1. The travelling allowance of a railway servant must be so regulated that it is not a source of profit to the recipient.
2. Travelling allowance forms part of the 'pay' of a railway servant for all purposes.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Travelling allowance must be regulated so that it is not a source of profit to the recipient, so statement 1 is correct; TA is not pay, so statement 2 is wrong.

q: The Centralised Pension Grievances Redress and Monitoring System, through which pensioners can lodge and track grievances relating to their pension matters online, is known as:

options.A: CPENGRAMS
options.B: ARPAN
options.C: UMID
options.D: SPARSH

e: CPENGRAMS is the Centralised Pension Grievances Redress and Monitoring System for pensioners to lodge and track pension grievances online.

q: A railway servant drawing basic pay of Rs 47,600 in Level 7 of the pay matrix is promoted to a post in Level 8. One increment is first granted to him in Level 7, taking his pay to the next cell of Rs 49,000, and his pay is then fixed in Level 8 at the cell equal to, or next above, that amount. His basic pay in Level 8 will be:
e: One increment in Level 7 takes pay from Rs 47,600 to Rs 49,000; Level 8 has a cell equal to Rs 49,000, so pay on promotion is fixed at Rs 49,000 under FR 22.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding restricted holidays:
1. A restricted holiday can be availed of by a railway servant only on a festival of the religion professed by him.
2. A restricted holiday can be availed of by a railway servant in combination with casual leave.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: A restricted holiday need not be only for a festival of the servant's own religion, so statement 1 is wrong; it can be availed in combination with casual leave, so only statement 2 is correct.

q: An annual increment of a railway servant falls due while he is under suspension. The correct position is that:

options.A: The increment is drawn by him on the due date as a matter of course
options.B: The increment is permanently forfeited on account of the suspension
options.C: Two increments are drawn by him on reinstatement, by way of compensation
options.D: The increment is not drawn during the period of suspension, and its drawal after reinstatement depends on the orders passed regarding the treatment of the period of suspension

e: An increment falling due during suspension is not drawn during suspension; its drawal after reinstatement depends on the orders on treatment of the suspension period.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding disability pension admissible under the extraordinary pension provisions:
1. Disability pension comprises a service element and a disability element.
2. The disability element is admissible only where the degree of disablement of the railway servant is 100 per cent.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Disability pension under extraordinary pension rules comprises a service element and a disability element, so statement 1 is correct; the disability element is proportionate to the degree of disablement and is not confined to 100 percent cases, so statement 2 is wrong.

q: Under Section 8(3) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, information relating to any occurrence or event which took place twenty years before the date on which the request is made shall be provided to the applicant, notwithstanding the exemptions contained in Section 8(1), except the exemptions contained in clauses:

options.A: (a), (b) and (c) of Section 8(1)
options.B: (d), (e) and (f) of Section 8(1)
options.C: (a), (c) and (i) of Section 8(1)
options.D: All the clauses of Section 8(1), without any exception

e: Section 8(3) of the RTI Act makes 20-year-old information disclosable despite Section 8(1), except clauses (a), (c) and (i) relating to sovereignty, privilege of legislatures and cabinet papers.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Travelling allowance on tour is admissible for a journey undertaken by a railway servant on duty away from his headquarters, from which he returns to his headquarters.
2. On transfer in public interest, besides travelling allowance for the journey, a railway servant is also entitled to other transfer benefits, such as Composite Transfer Grant and joining time, in accordance with the rules.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: TA on tour is admissible for a duty journey away from headquarters with return to headquarters, and on transfer in public interest CTG and joining time are also admissible, so both statements are correct.

q: At the request of a railway servant, the authority competent to grant leave may convert one kind of leave already availed of by him into another kind of leave, provided that:

options.A: The railway servant refunds the whole of the leave salary already drawn by him
options.B: The other kind of leave was due and admissible to him at the time the leave originally granted was availed of
options.C: The Railway Board sanctions the conversion in every case
options.D: The conversion is sought only within one year before his retirement

e: Conversion of one kind of leave already availed into another is allowed only if the other kind of leave was due and admissible at the time the original leave was availed.

q: In the matter of reservation of vacancies, the correct position in regard to a cadre consisting of a single post is that:

options.A: The single post is treated as reserved for Scheduled Castes by rotation
options.B: The single post is treated as reserved for Other Backward Classes
options.C: Reservation is applied to the single post and the vacancy is carried forward if it remains unfilled
options.D: Reservation cannot be applied to a single post, as a lone post in a cadre cannot be treated as a reserved post

e: Reservation cannot be applied to a single post in a cadre, as a lone post cannot be treated as a reserved post.

q: A railway servant covered under the National Pension System draws basic pay of Rs 30,000 per month and Dearness Allowance at the rate of 50 per cent. The monthly contribution payable by the railway servant himself to his Tier-I account, at 10 per cent of basic pay plus Dearness Allowance, will be:
e: Employee NPS contribution is 10 percent of Basic Pay plus DA: (Rs 30,000 + Rs 15,000) x 10/100 = Rs 45,000 x 10/100 = Rs 4,500 per month.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, premises whereon a manufacturing process is carried on are a 'factory' where the number of workers working on the premises is:

options.A: Five or more with the aid of power, or ten or more without the aid of power
options.B: Ten or more with the aid of power, or twenty or more without the aid of power
options.C: Fifty or more, whether power is used or not
options.D: One hundred or more, whether power is used or not

e: Under Section 2(m) of the Factories Act, premises are a factory if 10 or more workers work with the aid of power, or 20 or more without the aid of power.

q: A railway servant is promoted to a higher post at a time when he is on leave. He becomes entitled to draw the pay of the higher post:

options.A: From the date of the order of his promotion
options.B: From the date on which he applied for the leave
options.C: From the first day of the month following his promotion
options.D: From the date on which he actually assumes charge of the higher post on his return from leave

e: A servant promoted while on leave is entitled to the pay of the higher post only from the date he actually assumes charge of it on return from leave.
